title: Maximum Bags With Full Capacity of Rocks
summary: Given n bags with capacities and current rock counts, plus a number of additional rocks, determine the maximum number of bags that can reach their full capacity by adding rocks to any of the bags.
statement: Given n bags with capacities and current rock counts, plus a number of additional rocks, determine the maximum number of bags that can reach their full capacity by adding rocks to any of the bags.
constraints: Bag i needs capacity[i]-rocks[i] additional rocks to become full.
Distribute at most additional_rocks rocks and maximize the number of full bags.
Already-full bags have zero cost and count toward the answer.
hints: Each full bag is an item worth one with cost equal to its deficit.
To maximize item count under a budget, buy deficits from smallest to largest.
Sort capacity-rocks; consume affordable deficits until the next exceeds remaining rocks.
An exchange replacing any chosen larger deficit with an unchosen smaller one preserves count and never costs more, proving greedy optimality.
editorial: An exchange replacing any chosen larger deficit with an unchosen smaller one preserves count and never costs more, proving greedy optimality.

tests.explanation: The deficits are one, one, zero, one; filling two one-deficit bags yields three full bags.
The large supply can fill every bag, so return three.
